title: Security Concepts and Controls

header.html: the official CompTIA Security+ SY0-801 V8 exam objectives, document version 2.0

html:
1The core ideas

Concept Meaning Example
Confidentiality Only authorized people can read the data Encrypting a customer file
Integrity Data is accurate and has not been changed without permission A hash that shows a file was altered
Availability Systems and data are usable when needed Backups and redundant servers

These three form the CIA triad. Every control protects at least one of them.

Authentication, authorization and accounting (AAA)

Step Question Example
Authentication Who are you? Password plus an app code
Authorization What may you do? Read-only access to a share
Accounting What did you do? Logs of sign-ins and changes

Non-repudiation means a person cannot deny an action. Digital signatures and audit logs give it.

Exam tip

. Authentication proves identity; authorization grants rights after that; accounting records activity. A digital signature gives integrity and non-repudiation.

2Security principles

  • Defense in depth: use several layers of controls so one failure does not expose everything.
  • Least privilege: give users and systems only the access needed for the task, and no more.
  • Zero Trust: never trust, always verify. No device or user is trusted because of its network location; every request is authenticated and authorized, and access is continuously evaluated.
  • Separation of duties: no one person controls a whole critical process. Beyond the objectives

3Control categories

Controls are grouped by how they are implemented.

Category Meaning Examples
Technical (logical) Done by technology Firewall, encryption, antivirus, access control lists
Managerial (administrative) Policies and oversight Risk assessments, security policies, awareness programs
Operational Done by people in daily work Guards, security awareness procedures, backup routines
Physical (environmental) Protect buildings and equipment Locks, fences, badges, cameras, fire suppression

4Control types

Controls are also grouped by what they do.

Type Purpose Examples
Preventive Stops an incident Firewall rule, door lock, patching
Deterring Discourages an attacker Warning signs, visible cameras, banners
Detective Finds an incident that happened IDS alerts, log review, motion sensors
Corrective Fixes the damage or restores Restoring from backup, patching after an attack
Compensating Substitutes when the main control cannot be used Extra monitoring on a legacy system that cannot be patched
Directive Instructs what must be done Policies, procedures, standards

Exam tip

. Ask two questions: how is it implemented (technical, managerial, operational, physical) and what does it do (preventive, deterring, detective, corrective, compensating, directive). A camera is physical and detective (and also deterring). A policy is managerial and directive.

Exam tip

. A compensating control is a substitute for a control that cannot be used. A corrective control happens after the event. Do not confuse them.

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1Fabrikam Outdoors adds a banner that warns that all activity on its network is monitored. Which control type is mainly shown?

  • ACorrective
  • BDeterring
  • CCompensating
  • DPreventive
Show the answer

Answer: B. A warning banner discourages misuse, which is a deterring control. It does not stop or fix anything.

S2A legacy server cannot be patched, so the team places it on an isolated segment with extra logging. Which control type is this?

  • ACompensating
  • BDirective
  • CCorrective
  • DDeterring
Show the answer

Answer: A. The isolation and logging substitute for patching that cannot be done, so they are compensating controls.

S3A company writes an acceptable use policy that tells staff what they must and must not do. Which category and type fit best?

  • ATechnical and preventive
  • BPhysical and detective
  • CManagerial and directive
  • DOperational and corrective
Show the answer

Answer: C. A policy is a managerial control that directs behavior, so it is a directive control.

S4Which concept is provided by a digital signature on a signed contract?

  • AAvailability and accounting
  • BIntegrity and non-repudiation
  • CObfuscation and masking
  • DAuthorization and accounting
Show the answer

Answer: B. A signature shows the content was not changed (integrity) and the signer cannot deny signing it (non-repudiation).

S5An administrator gives a help desk analyst only the rights needed to reset passwords. Which principle is applied?

  • ADefense in depth
  • BLeast privilege
  • CZero Trust
  • DNon-repudiation
Show the answer

Answer: B. Granting only the access needed for the task is least privilege.

S6A user signs in and the system then checks which files the user may open. Which step of AAA is the file check?

  • AAccounting
  • BAuthentication
  • CAuthorization
  • DAttestation
Show the answer

Answer: C. Deciding what the authenticated user may access is authorization.

5.2 Recall questions

R1What are the three parts of the CIA triad?

Show the answer

Confidentiality, integrity and availability.

R2What does AAA stand for?

Show the answer

Authentication, authorization and accounting.

R3Name the four control categories.

Show the answer

Technical, managerial, operational and physical.

R4Name the six control types.

Show the answer

Preventive, deterring, detective, corrective, compensating and directive.

R5What is the slogan of Zero Trust?

Show the answer

Never trust, always verify.

R6What does non-repudiation prevent?

Show the answer

A person denying an action they performed.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
CIA confidentiality (secret), integrity (unchanged), availability (usable)
AAA who you are, what you may do, what you did; non-repudiation by signatures and logs
Principles defense in depth, least privilege, Zero Trust (verify every request)
Categories technical, managerial, operational, physical
Types preventive stops, deterring discourages, detective finds, corrective fixes, compensating substitutes, directive instructs
